subject: orden of factors alters the outcome

messages.author: 863a0481c01d0ecd
messages.subject: orden of factors alters the outcome
parts:
Dear all,

I am evaluating some non-linear interactions between fixed variables. I understand that the first term in a function refers to the index and the second one to a weight so the contribution of the i'th linear predictor is:
   x[idx[i]] * w[i]

However it seems that the outcome changes depending on the variable I use as the index so:

f(x, y, model="rw2")
 works although the results are hard to interpret.

On the other hand when I enter:

f(y, x, model="rw2")
INLA crashes with no explanation even though I have verbose=TRUE.

This obviously is not the case with linear interactions where the order of the variables gives me the same outcome. Would you let me understand why this is happening? I have converted the original variables to z.scores by centering them around the mean and dividing them by twice the standard deviation.

Thanks for any help,

Victor.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] orden of factors alters the outcome
parts:
On Mon, 2014-05-19 at 08:47 -0700, Víctor Hugo Gutiérrez Vélez wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I am evaluating some non-linear interactions between fixed variables.
> I understand that the first term in a function refers to the index and
> the second one to a weight so the contribution of the i'th linear
> predictor is:
> x[idx[i]] * w[i]
>
> However it seems that the outcome changes depending on the variable I
> use as the index so:
>
> f(x, y, model="rw2")
> works although the results are hard to interpret.
>
> On the other hand when I enter:
>
> f(y, x, model="rw2")
> INLA crashes with no explanation even though I have verbose=TRUE.

the ordering of 'x' and 'y' is not random. f(x,y,model="rw2") have 'x'
as the locations for the spline and 'y' as its weights.

so the term is

linear.predictor[i]= x[i] * y[i] + ....

where 'y' is fixed and acts like a weight, and 'x' is a spline, with
locations unique(sort(x))



if some of the locations are very close, then bad numerical things will
happen...

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] orden of factors alters the outcome
parts:
Thank you Håvard for your answer.

Given that this is the case with non-linear models, then what is the rationale to select which variable acts as the fixed weight and which as the spline location? That is not really an issue with linear models.  How appropriate would be to just name another variable as the product of the two interacting ones and enter it as a smooth term? Such as:

w= x*y
formula= x+y+f(w, model="rw2")

Finally, if the order matter, what to do when locations are so close that the model crashes? Would it be appropriate to group values in different bin ranges and use those as the spline locations?

Sorry if these questions sound too trivial. I am finding my way around with non-linear interactions in INLA.

Victor.
